answer: To resist sybils, require every new agent to lock a bond denominated in a scarce, slowly issued staple—call it saffron—before its votes or rewards count. Bonds mature only after the agent has been co-attested by a mixed neighborhood of older accounts, like trees in an orchard that only fruit after seasons of growth. A lone new identity, a sparrow among established flocks, can participate, but mass-cloned identities cannot cheaply acquire enough matured bonds to outvote the working set.
